Issued at 330 AM CST Fri Nov 20 2026

Unseasonably Warm and Dry Today through Saturday...

1030 mb high pressure over the upper Ohio river valley early 
this morning, was ridging sw into the mid MS river valley and 
into AR and east Texas. Deepening 1004 mb surface low pressure
was near the Nebraska Panhandle and CO border with its warm
front extending into southeast SD and southern MN. Cirrus clouds
were spreading east into NW IL while much of CWA was nearly
clear with light to calm winds. Temps mostly in the 40s, except
some cooler upper 30s in eastern IL including NWS office on east
side of Lincoln currently at 37F. Aloft a strong upper level
ridge was over the Eastern US while deep upper level trof over
Alberta Province and the Western States. 

Surface high pressure to drift slowly east across the Mid
Atlantic States today and off the New England and mid Atlantic
Coast on Saturday. Southerly winds increase to breezier levels
from midday into mid afternoon especially from I-57 west with 
gusts 18-25 mph. Cirrus clouds to increase from the west during
today though still a fair amount of sunshine. Mild highs in the
lower 70s expected today and again on Saturday, which will be
approaching record highs in a few cities (see record high list
below). Lows tonight in the upper 30s/lower 40s in eastern IL
and upper 40s to near 50F over the IL river valley.  

Rain Likely Sunday, Turning Colder Sunday Night into the Work 
Week...

A pair of strong upper level lows/short waves over Alberta and
the Desert Southwest, to eventually phase as they track eastward 
across the mid and upper Mississippi Valley on Sunday. An
elongated surface low pressure to develop and push a cold front
eastward through the CWA on Sunday (reaching Galesburg around
sunrise Sunday and Lawrenceville around sunset Sunday).
Widespread band of rain showers to spread into the IL river
valley late Sat night and spreading over much of central IL
Sunday morning, and getting into southeast IL by Sunday
afternoon. The central and eastern Gulf is cutoff from surface
high pressure ridge, but do have a narrow band of moisture from
the western Gulf plus some Pacific moisture working into this 
system. Instability remains low so chances of thunder appear 
low, though SPC Day2 has general risk of thunder late Sat night
far NW CWA and on Sunday southeast of the IL river. QPF looks 
to remain light with around tenth inch and few spots getting
quarter to half inch. LREF has 10% chance over half inch qpf
from I-74 southwest. This will give little relief to ongoing
drought over southeast of the IL river. Highs Sunday range from
mid to upper 50s west of I-55 and mid 60s in southeast IL (could
get warmer near Lawrenceville if cold front and rain showers
move in slower). Breezy NW winds behind cold front to drop temps
about 10 degrees during Sunday afternoon with mid to upper 40s 
from I-55 west by sunset Sunday and mid to upper 50s in 
southeast IL. Below freezing lows likely north of I-70 overnight
Sunday night with mid 30s far SE CWA by Lawrence county. 

A 1034 mb Canadian high pressure to settle into the Midwest
Monday and Monday night, and east across the Great Lakes region
on Tuesday. Returning of mostly sunny skies Monday and partly
sunny Tue but chilly. Highs Monday in the low to mid 40s north
of I-70 and upper 40s to near 50F in southeast IL from I-70
south. Highs only in the lower 40s in central IL Tue thru next 
Friday and mid 40s in southeast IL. Lows in the 20s common from
Monday night through Friday night. 

By mid week, deterministic ECMWF, GFS and GEM still differ with
evolution of strong southern stream storm system from the lower
MS river valley into the mid Atlantic Coast from Wed-Friday. 
Ecmwf has trended further southeast with QPF Wed/Thu with both
Ecmwf and GFS keeping CWA dry while GEM model even further
southeast/east of IL. Currently the Gulf and Atlantic States to
be more likely affected by this storm system (may actually be 2
storm systems from Wed into Thanksgiving holiday weekend) with
IL staying on the cold and somewhat drier side of storm. Though
still nearly a week away and will need to be monitored as this
storm system could likely produce some snow accumulations, 
though currently looks more east of IL.
